messages:
maya: quick idea — propose we centralize span identity (canonical_span_id) and move heavy billing/cost attributes off the span payload into a joinable cost table. goal: reduce span cardinality and speed joins for cost queries.

jonah: :eyes: can you sketch the migration steps? worried about queries that currently rely on inline tags.

maya: short sketch: 1) add canonical_span_id header/attr that SDKs write for new spans. 2) introduce a cost_mapping service that maps canonical_span_id -> billing_key (and lifecycle). 3) traces keep only lightweight refs; analytics queries join against cost_mapping when needed. 4) dual-write during migration for ~30d.

liam: that sounds promising. how do we handle sampling? if sampled-out spans lose cost context we break chargebacks.

maya: two options: a) ensure cost_mapping is written upstream to a persistent store independent of sampling, b) introduce a compact delta record that carries minimal billing_key for sampled spans. prefer (a) to keep span payload light.

arjun: question about cardinality — won't canonical_span_id itself be high-cardinality? why better than current tags?

maya: good Q — canonical_span_id is a UUID per trace/span (same as current span id) but we dedupe billing information into cost_mapping which is coarse (tenant + product + feature flags) so the join key points to a small set of billing rows. we avoid storing the full billing attribute map on each span. net storage + index reduction.

sophia: how does this interact with downstream enrichment pipelines? we currently enrich spans with user/tenant attrs at ingress.

maya: ingress still annotates spans with canonical_span_id and a minimal shard_key. enrichment job writes/updates the cost_mapping table (idempotent). downstream consumers can either join or fetch billing info on demand.

jonah: runtime concerns: joins during ad-hoc queries can be heavy. we should add a cache layer in the query path and pre-aggregate common rollups. also pre-populate cost_mapping for active tenants.

liam: logging and debugging experience — ops wants to still see billing on span in SLO views. plan for fallback: the UI can resolve billing via mapping service during render, with a cache TTL. if service unavailable, show "billing: unknown" and surface fallback counters.

maya: prototype config snippet for SDK header (we'll roll through our python/go/ts libs):
```
# SDK pseudocode
span.set_attribute("canonical_span_id", span.id)
http.headers["x-rd-canonical-span"] = span.id
```

maya: migration checklist (WIP):
- add header & SDK update (minor semver)
- enrichment job writes cost_mapping (idempotent)
- dual-write: spans keep old billing tags + new minimal refs for 30d
- analytics queries opt-in to join cost_mapping
- roll UI fallback to resolve via mapping service
- remove inline billing tags after verification window

arjun: for verification we should build a diff-job to compare cost attribution results between old inline-tags vs new join method across a sample window. that will catch edge cases.

jonah: agree. also create a query-performance dashboard: join latency, cache hit rate, mapping write QPS.

tracing-bot: FYI — meeting created: Observability: Span Identity & Cost Mapping, Thu 16:00. Invite sent to @maya @jonah @liam @sophia @arjun. Link: https://meet.redwood.host/obs-span-mapping

sophia: action items for meeting: 1) pick migration window, 2) owners for SDK, enrichment, mapping service, UI, 3) define verification queries, 4) plan rollback criteria.

maya: assigning owners in thread draft: SDK: @liam, enrichment: @sophia, mapping service: @arjun, analytics: @jonah, UI: @maya. I'll add to the RFC doc.

liam: quick note — SDK changes should be opt-out via env var so infra teams can flip early for testing.

maya: agreed. thanks all. will add draft RFC link after the meeting. :+1:
